The bastide was pulled down in 1673, and the arch went up the next year." Delete the 1862 listing and the 1988 restoration.

issues: period: the whole text is the triumphal arch of 1673, not the medieval gate the card is about, and the card's own note says so. | source: history_fr holds only the article's lead; the article's Historique describes the gate the map shows. | consistency: the summary already says Louis XIV replaced the gate in 1672-1673, so the detail restates it and adds only the arch. | voice: the last sentence has no main verb ("Regarded as one of the most representative monuments...").
evidence: fr.wikipedia, "Porte Saint-Denis", section Historique (read as wikitext, 3 Nov 2026), https://fr.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Porte_Saint-Denis&action=raw: "La troisieme porte Saint-Denis, ou << bastide Saint-Denis >>, du [XIVe siecle], se trouvait 60 metres au sud de l'actuel arc de triomphe", and of the fourth, "a l'emplacement d'une porte medievale dans l'enceinte de Charles V". The same article dates the arch 1673 in its lead and "erigee en 1672" in its Historique, so the source contradicts itself on the year. Cited there to Gagneux and Prouvost, Sur les traces des enceintes de Paris, Parigramme, 2004, and to Perouse de Montclos, Histoire de l'architecture francaise, vol. II, pp. 317-318.
suggested_edit: Rewrite from the Historique: "The gate on the map was the third of the name, a 14th-century bastide of the wall of Charles V standing some 60 metres south of where the arch now is." Delete the whole of the present text, which is about the arch.

issues: consistency: beyond the Bussy spelling the detail restates the short description above it - the gate's position by the carrefour de l'Odeon, the 13th-century build and the 17th-century demolition are all already there. | voice: 44 words of which the one new fact is a variant spelling.
suggested_edit: Keep "Also recorded under the spelling Bussy, it was one of the two gates called the portes Saint-Germain, the other being the porte des Cordeliers" and drop the rest, or return null: the source is a single sentence and the summary has spent it.

issues: consistency: the detail adds nothing to the short description, which already gives the porte des Cordeliers name, the carrefour de l'Odeon, the 13th century and the 17th-century demolition. | voice: a 52-word restatement.
suggested_edit: Return null. One garbled sentence of source cannot carry both a summary and a detail, and the summary has it.

issues: period: half the text is 1762-1811, and the summary already says the fair ran until the Revolution and that the Marche Saint-Germain stands on its site. | voice: "gradually integrated into the urban fabric of Paris" is the source's phrase translated whole and says less in English than in French.
suggested_edit: Cut the 1811 demolition, which the summary has. Lead on the fair the map shows: outside the wall, more than 120 loges, and the 15th-century buildings that stood until the fire of 1762.

issues: overclaim: "the cartographer Dheulland" - the register says only "Dheulland la nomme rue des Cordelieres"; the trade is the detail's addition, the same habit as "the mapmaker Lacaille" at L0262 and "Henri Sauval" at L0319. | period: the back half is the 1938 and 1944 renamings, both of which the summary already names, and the 12th-century creation the source gives is dropped.
suggested_edit: Write "Dheulland", and keep the 12th century the source states: "Created in the 12th century, the street was part of the old rue de Lourcine, written Loursine, l'Oursine, l'Orsine, l'Ursine and, by Jaillot, Lorcines; it was also the rue du Clos Ganay and the rue de la Franchise, and Dheulland names it rue des Cordelieres." Cut the 1938 and 1944 sentences.

issues: overclaim: three additions the register does not make - "the historian La Tynna", "Felix Lazare" (the 1844 dictionary is by the brothers Felix and Louis Lazare), and, worse, "Later sources distinguished it from other streets of the same name", which invents the reason the saints' names were added. Streets of the same name are the project's known trap, and a guess about why one was distinguished from another is exactly what should not be written.
evidence: The attribution is settled from fr.wikipedia, "Rue Greneta" (read 3 Nov 2026), which cites "Felix et Louis Lazare, Dictionnaire administratif et historique des rues de Paris et de ses monuments" and refers to "Les freres Lazare"; the same two-author form is used in the references of fr.wikipedia, "Ville l'Eveque" (edition de 1844, p. 403), which is a source this project already holds.
suggested_edit: "La Tynna has it as the rue Percee Saint-Paul in 1816; the Lazare brothers' dictionary of 1844 as the rue Percee Saint-Antoine." Drop the sentence about distinguishing it from other streets.

issues: period: the last two sentences are the 1885 transfer of a section to the rue du Pont-Louis-Philippe. | voice: the body is a list of eight former names with nothing said about the street. | consistency: the summary already gives the 13th-century deeds, the rue de la Couture du Temple and the rue Barbette.
suggested_edit: Cut the 1885 sentence and keep the names that are not in the summary, with what they mean: the Culture and Cloture du Temple from the Templars' ground it ran to, the Poterne Barbette from the postern in Philip Augustus's wall.

issues: period: the last two sentences are the 1885 transfer. | consistency: this card is probably a second label on the same street as L0238 and carries a near-identical list of names, so the site says the same thing twice. | voice: a list of eight former names and an administrative order.
suggested_edit: Return null. The card's own point - that the map seems to label one street twice, and that Guillot called it simply the rue du Temple - is in the summary, and a second copy of L0238's name list adds nothing.

issues: overclaim: "The mapmaker Lacaille" - the source says only "Lacaille", and Jean de La Caille was a printer-bookseller who published a plan, not a mapmaker; the trade is the detail's own addition. | period: six of the seven dates are 1768, 1793, 1806 and 1808; the 14th-century name and the 1328 ruelle au Villain, which are the map-relevant part, get one clause each.
evidence: data.bnf.fr, authority record for Jean de La Caille (1645-1723), https://data.bnf.fr/12192872/jean_de_la_caille/fr.pdf: he is recorded as an imprimeur-libraire who succeeded Denis II Thierry as printer-bookseller to the police in 1712, and the Description de la ville et des fauxbourgs de Paris en vingt planches (1714) is listed under him in that capacity. So "Lacaille" in the street register is an authority who published a plan in twenty plates, which is not the same as being its maker.
suggested_edit: "Lacaille writes rue Courtauvillain, and rue or ruelle Auvillain" - give him no trade. Lead on the 1328 ruelle au Villain and the rue du Seigneur de Montmorency, and compress the 1768-1808 renamings into one clause.

issues: consistency: the card is the rue de l'Homme-Arme and it gets one sentence; the other five are the rue des Deux Portes, the rue des Billettes and the rue du Chaume group. The armed man's shop sign, which is the card's own subject, is in the summary and is never picked up. | overclaim: "rue des Jardins in the 13th century" drops the source's "a la fin du".
suggested_edit: Give the card's street the body of the text, and name the others only as the neighbouring sections they are: "The rue de l'Homme-Arme ran between the rue Sainte-Croix-de-la-Bretonnerie and the rue des Blancs-Manteaux; the sections joined to it to the south had been the rue des Deux Portes, known as rue Entre Deux Portes in the late 13th century, and the rue des Billettes, the rue des Jardins at the same date."

issues: source: the detail copies the register's bowdlerised entry as a street name - "rue Trace put...", ellipsis and all - which reads on the card as a broken word rather than a name. | source: the list of the rue Transnonain's names stops one short and never reaches "rue Transnonnain", the card's own name, which the source gives as the last of the series ("et enfin, rue Transnonnain"). | period: the closing sentence is the 1972 clearance for the Centre national d'art contemporain.
suggested_edit: Drop "rue Trace put..." rather than print a truncation, and close the series properly: "...rue Trousse Nonnain, rue Tasse Nonnain and at last rue Transnonnain." Cut the 1972 sentence. The opening - a street of the late 11th century crossing the city wall, called rue de la Poterne inside it and rue outre la Poterne Nicolas Hydron outside - is the best material here and should lead.

issues: period: two of the four sentences are the 1865 and 1869 renamings of stretches into the rue Linne and the rue Jussieu. | consistency: the one period fact the register carries - that the street was already there when the abbey was founded - is dropped, and the register dates that foundation to the 11th century where the site's own summary and card L0049 say the 12th; the clash should have gone in notes.
suggested_edit: Keep the course from the rue Copeau to the place Maubert and the rue du Faubourg Saint-Victor name, cut the 1865 and 1869 sentences, and flag the 11th/12th-century clash to the maintainer rather than writing either date.

issues: overclaim: "During the Revolutionary era, from 1793 until 1815" - 1815 is the Restoration, and the source gives only the span, not a label for it.
suggested_edit: "It was simply the rue de la Montagne from 1793 to 1815." The 1266-1276 attestation is the useful new fact here and reads well.

issues: consistency: the card is the western stretch - its summary is the lord of Montmorency's street and Flamel's house - and the detail is entirely about the eastern stretch between the rue Beaubourg and the rue du Temple, which is the neighbouring card L0262; a reader is told "This eastern segment adopted the name rue de Montmorency in 1768" on a card whose own street carried that name from the 14th century. | overclaim: "the entire street was renamed the rue de la Reunion" - the source's "elle" is the eastern part under discussion, and the register does not say the whole street took the name. | overclaim: "The cartographer Lacaille", as at L0262.
evidence: data.bnf.fr, authority record for Jean de La Caille (1645-1723), https://data.bnf.fr/12192872/jean_de_la_caille/fr.pdf: imprimeur-libraire, printer-bookseller to the police from 1712, under whom the Description de la ville et des fauxbourgs de Paris en vingt planches (1714) is listed. The register's "Lacaille" is a published authority, not a cartographer. The split of the street is the register's own: "La partie situee entre les rues Saint-Martin et Beaubourg... rue du Seigneur de Montmorency. La partie situee entre les rues Beaubourg et du Temple... la ruelle au Villain."
suggested_edit: Write this card from its own stretch: "From the 14th century the part between the rue Saint-Martin and the rue Beaubourg was the rue du Seigneur de Montmorency, after the lord whose house stood on it." Then, if the eastern stretch is mentioned at all, say plainly that it is the neighbouring section. Cut "the entire street" and Lacaille's trade.

issues: overclaim: three additions the source does not make - "Henri" Sauval (the register says only "Sauval"), "the 16th-century map of the Tapisserie" (the register gives no date, and published datings of the plan de la Tapisserie range over c. 1540, 1547 and c. 1550, with the tapestry itself about 1571), and "briefly" of the 1851 designation. | voice: the street is called "the passage" in the third sentence, a word the source does not use.
evidence: No page on the plan de la Tapisserie was opened and read, so its dating is reported from catalogue descriptions seen in search results only (Princeton's facsimile record labels it 1547, a Merian caption c. 1540 with the tapestry c. 1571, a dealer listing c. 1550). The finding is that the source gives no date, not that 16th-century is wrong. Marked shallow for that reason.
suggested_edit: "Sauval claims it was once called the rue du Croc; the plan de la Tapisserie gives it the name la Radrerie." Drop "Henri", "16th-century", "briefly" and "passage".

issues: consistency: the detail contains no fact the short description does not already carry - the course between the rue de la Bucherie and the rue Galande, the names rue du Pave de la place Maubert and rue d'Amboise, and the 1806-1912 merger are all in the summary. | overclaim: "before being separated again and subsequently given its modern designation" is an inference the register does not state.
suggested_edit: Return null. The register entry is three sentences and the summary has spent all three.

issues: period: the text closes on a 1974 extension of the place Alphonse-Laveran in front of a military hospital, on a card about the cardo of Lutetia and the road to Compostela. | voice: "this major Left Bank arterial road" is traffic-engineering English; and the list of grand'rue names stops before reaching "grand'rue Saint-Jacques", which the source gives as the last of the series.
suggested_edit: Cut the 1974 clause, write "this great Left Bank street", and close the list where the source does: "...grand'rue vers Saint-Matelin, grand'rue Saint-Benoit, and at last grand'rue Saint-Jacques."

issues: overclaim: "Jean Boisseau" - the register says only "Boisseau", and the first name is the detail's addition, the same habit as Lacaille, Sauval and Ducerceau elsewhere in this set.
suggested_edit: Write "Boisseau". Otherwise this entry is sound: the hedge on Jean le Maitre is kept, the names are in order, and the Cholets college's own street is the subject throughout.

issues: consistency: the summary already says the rue du Renard-Saint-Sauveur and the rue Beaurepaire were joined to it in 1868, and the detail opens with that merger and then spends two of its three sentences on those two streets rather than on the rue d'Arnetal the card is about. | period: the opening sentence is the 1868 order.
suggested_edit: Open on the card's own street: "Earlier forms of the name run rue d'Arnetal, Darnetal, Dernetat, Drenetat and Darnestat, and it was also called the rue de la Trinite." Then the two absorbed streets in one sentence each, with their 1255 and 1313 dates.

issues: overclaim: "The cartographer Lacaille" adds a trade the register does not give (see L0262); "it was originally called the rue Macra Madiana" hardens the source's conditional "elle se serait appelee", and adds "originally"; "later recorded it as" adds a sequence the register does not give. | period: the closing two clauses are the 1806 and 1814 renamings, and the 1786 edict on the riverside houses - the one thing here about the street as a place - is left to the summary.
suggested_edit: "Older deeds are said to have called it the rue Macra Madiana; Lacaille names it the rue de la Vieille Pelleterie, a name it already bore in 1183." Cut the Desaix renaming.

issues: voice: a list of former names; the one thing in it that bears on the map - "several 16th-century maps label it rue Serpente" - is buried mid-sentence and is the best line in the entry. | consistency: the summary already gives the 1179 opening, the 1180 vicus Serpentis and the 1851 absorption of the rue du Battoir.
suggested_edit: Lead on the map: "Several 16th-century plans, this one among them, write it rue Serpente; a deed of 1263 has the Latin Vicus Tortuosus, the winding street." Then the Battoir names, shorter.

issues: period: both sentences are after the map - the 1792 rue Catinat, the return in 1802, and a 1934 absorption into the place Paul-Painleve. Everything the register has from before 1550, the 13th-century rue des Deux-Portes, the rue Sorbonne of about 1281 and Guillot's rue aux Hoirs de Sabonnes, is in the summary and the detail steps over all of it. | voice: 42 words, at the floor, of register administration.
suggested_edit: Return null. Once the summary has taken the 13th century, this register entry has nothing left but renamings.

issues: source: the 1864 imperial decree named it rue Gerson AND rue Restaut, which is the register's own first line; the detail gives only rue Gerson, so the reader is told the street became one thing when the source says it became two. The decree also created a place Gerson ("rue et place Gerson"). | voice: "Later identified as the rue Grenouiller or Grenouillière on Abbe Delagrive's map" imposes a date the source does not give - the register lists Delagrive last but assigns him no period.
suggested_edit: "An imperial decree of 24 August 1864 divided it into the rue Gerson and the rue Restaut." Drop "Later" before Delagrive. The 1236 and 1254 Argenteuil names and the 1443 rue aux Ecoliers de Rethel are the strongest part of this entry and should keep their room.

issues: source: "The middle section, formerly the rue Beaurepaire between the rue Dussoubs and the rue Montorgueil" is wrong - Beaurepaire is the western end, and the middle section is the rue du Renard-Saint-Sauveur, which is this card's own street. | consistency: the card is the rue du Renard-Saint-Sauveur and the detail never says what that street was; its 1313 rue Percee and 1383 rue du Renard appear only in the short description. | period: the text opens on the 1868 merger.
evidence: fr.wikipedia, "Rue Greneta" (read as wikitext, 3 Nov 2026), https://fr.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rue_Greneta&action=raw: the street "commence au 241, rue Saint-Martin et se termine au 72, rue Montorgueil", and its cross streets are listed "d'Est en Ouest" as boulevard de Sebastopol, rue de Palestro, rue Saint-Denis, rue Dussoubs. With the register's own three ranges - Greneta Saint-Martin to Saint-Denis, Renard-Saint-Sauveur Saint-Denis to Dussoubs, Beaurepaire Dussoubs to Montorgueil - the order east to west is Greneta, Renard, Beaurepaire, so the card's street is the middle one. Article cites Felix et Louis Lazare, Dictionnaire administratif et historique des rues de Paris, and Jean de La Tynna, Dictionnaire topographique... des rues de Paris, 1817.
suggested_edit: Put the card's own street first and fix the position: "Between the rue Saint-Denis and the rue Dussoubs, the street existed in 1313 as the rue Percee, then Perciee, and was the rue du Renard by 1383. In 1868 it became the middle section of the rue Greneta, with the rue Beaurepaire to the west and the old rue Greneta to the east."

issues: consistency: the card is the rue Montorgueil itself and the detail is wholly about the rue au Comte-d'Artois, the neighbouring label L0381, with no sentence saying how the two relate; the mont Orgueil the street climbs is never mentioned. | overclaim: "permanently merged" - the source says only that it was joined again in 1830.
suggested_edit: Say at the start that this is the stretch joined to the rue Montorgueil, not the rue Montorgueil itself, and drop "permanently". Better: write this card from the hill and the market and leave the Comte-d'Artois names to L0381.

issues: consistency: the card is the rue Pavee and it gets one sentence of four; the rest is the rue du Petit-Lion and the old rue Tiquetonne. The first list also drops "rue du Petit Lion" and "rue de l'Arbalete ou rue des Arbaletriers", which are in the source. | overclaim: "the rue Paule on Ducerceau's map" is fine, but see L0406 on expanding the name.
suggested_edit: Lead with the card's street: "Between the rue Dussoubs and the rue Montorgueil the street was the rue Pavee from 1313, and kept that name until 1851, when it was joined to the rue du Petit-Lion." Then the other sections briefly.

issues: consistency: the summary already has the 1792 merger into the rue Montorgueil, which the detail repeats as its opening. | overclaim: "briefly returned" and "permanently reincorporated" are the detail's own judgements; the source gives only the three dates.
suggested_edit: Drop "briefly" and "permanently" and lead on the names: "The stretch between the rue Montmartre and the rue Mauconseil was first the rue Nicolas Arrode, then the rue au Comte - or a la Comtesse - d'Artois, and the rue de la Porte au Comte d'Artois."

issues: overclaim: "the eastern stretch between the rue Mondetour and the rue Saint-Denis" - the register gives no direction, and the brief warns against supplying them. | period: the text opens on the 1792-1806 Bonconseil renaming, which the summary already names.
suggested_edit: Drop "eastern" and lead on the map-relevant fact instead: "On Merian's plan the part between the rue Mondetour and the rue Saint-Denis is called the rue Saint-Jacques de l'Hopital; the street formerly ran that far."

issues: period: the only fact the detail adds to the summary is the 1936 incorporation of a section into the Halles Centrales; the oven that gave the street its name, which is what the label means, is left to the summary. | consistency (not the detail's fault, but on the same card): the short description calls Vauvilliers "the architect" - he was a Hellenist scholar who handled Paris's food supply in 1789.
evidence: fr.wikipedia, "Rue Vauvilliers" (read as wikitext, 3 Nov 2026), https://fr.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Rue_Vauvilliers&action=raw: "Depuis 1864, elle tient son nom du savant helleniste Jean-Francois Vauvilliers (1737-1801)", "qui assura les approvisionnements alimentaires de Paris en 1789" - a Hellenist, not an architect. The same article has the street's own century: it "existait deja en 1238", was the "rue du Four-de-la-Couture-de-l'Eveque" in 1255, and the bishop's four banal stood "au bout de la rue du cote de l'eglise Saint-Eustache" and worked from 1137 until about 1410.
suggested_edit: Replace the 1936 sentence with the oven: "The bishop's communal oven that gave the street its name stood at the Saint-Eustache end and was in use from 1137 until about 1410, so by the time of this map the name had outlived the oven." Separately, fix "the architect Vauvilliers" in the short description.

issues: consistency: four of the five sentences are the rue du Battoir-Saint-Andre, a different street, on a card whose summary is only about the rue Serpente; this card is also a second label on the street L0365 covers, and the two details overlap heavily. | voice: a list of former names.
suggested_edit: Return null, or keep only the rue Serpente: the 1263 Vicus Tortuosus and the 16th-century plans that write it rue Serpente. The rue du Battoir belongs on L0365, which at least has the 1851 merger in its summary.

issues: consistency: the detail's chronology contradicts the short description above it - the summary has Guillot calling it the rue des Cordeles in 1300, the detail says it was the rue Saint-Germain before 1672 and the rue des Cordeliers only from 1672 to 1690. The register carries both and the author should have flagged the clash rather than presenting the later sequence flatly. | period: of seven dated statements, one is before 1550.
suggested_edit: Say what the register actually leaves unresolved: "Guillot already called it the rue des Cordeles in 1300, after the Franciscan convent, and in 1304 deeds name it for Saint-Come and Saint-Damien; the register then has it as the rue Saint-Germain before 1672 and the rue des Cordeliers only from 1672 to 1690." Cut the Revolution renamings and the boulevard Saint-Germain absorption.

issues: overclaim: "Henri Sauval" and "Jacques Androuet du Cerceau" - the source writes only "Sauval" and "Ducerceau", and the first names and the identification are the detail's own additions, which the brief forbids adding silently. | consistency: the card is the original rue Tiquetonne and it gets the last sentence only; the first three are the rue du Petit-Lion and the rue Pavee. The baker Roger Tiquetonne of 1399, the card's own subject, is in the summary and never picked up.
evidence: Henri Sauval (1623-1676) and Jacques Androuet du Cerceau are the usual referents, so the expansions are probably right - but they are not in the supplied register text, and the project has already been burnt by a plausible addition (quote_verification.md, the four contradicted claims). No independent source was opened to fix which Ducerceau plan the register means; the finding is that the source does not say.
suggested_edit: Write "Sauval" and "Ducerceau", as the register does, and open on the rue Tiquetonne itself: "Before the rue Etienne-Marcel was cut through, the rue Tiquetonne ran between the rue Montorgueil and the rue Montmartre; it was the rue Denis le Coffrier in 1372 and the rue Quiquetonne in 1400."

issues: overclaim: "Jacques Androuet du Cerceau recorded it as Cernelles" - the register says only "Ducerceau ecrit Cernelles"; the first names and the identification are added. | voice: the detail is a bare list of spelling variants with no statement about the street, which is what the brief's third trap warns against.
evidence: Same as L0406: the expansion is probable but is not in the supplied text, and no independent source was opened that fixes which Ducerceau the register's street entries mean. The register's own words are "Ducerceau ecrit Cernelles".
suggested_edit: Write "Ducerceau". And give the reader the street rather than the list: the source's "Cette voie existait au XIIIe siecle" and the two sections' extents carry more than six variant spellings do.

issues: voice: "later Behaigne or Vieille Behaigne, references to Bohemia in 1328" reads as though something was referred to in 1328; the source means the name Behaigne, Bohemia, is attested in 1328. | consistency: the 1888 clearance for the rue du Louvre is in the summary, and the detail gives it plus the 1890 order as its closing two clauses.
suggested_edit: "...later Behaigne, from Bohemia, recorded in 1328, and Vieille Behaigne." Cut the last sentence. The 16th-century names of the Filles Repenties and the Filles Penitentes are the map-century fact here and deserve more than a clause.

issues: voice: the variant list prints "d'Autruche or d'Autruche dite du Louvre", repeating one form and dropping "de l'Autruche", which the source has between them. | consistency: the 1664 enlargement and the survival as the rue de l'Oratoire are both in the summary.
suggested_edit: "...Autheriche, then d'Autruche, de l'Autruche and d'Autruche dite du Louvre." The two dates the summary lacks - rue du Louvre in 1600, and the rue de l'Oratoire still called rue de l'Autruche in 1732 - are worth keeping and should lead.

issues: consistency: the card is the rue de Grenelle-Saint-Honore and the detail calls it "One section", then gives the other section equal room; the summary already has the 13th-century date and Ducerceau's "Cernelles". | voice: 47 words that are a list of variants and nothing else.
suggested_edit: Return null, or write the card's own stretch: "Running as far as the rue Coquilliere, the street appears as rue de Guernelles, Guarnelle, Guarnales and Garnelles before settling as rue de Grenelle-Saint-Honore." The rue Maverse and the rue Platriere belong to L0408.

issues: consistency: the summary already gives the 1212 rue des Chanoines, the rue Saint-Thomas-du-Louvre and the suppression for the Louvre, so the detail is largely the same four facts reordered, with 1242 and the Revolution name added. | period: three of its four statements are 1808 or later.
suggested_edit: Keep "First documented as the rue des Chanoines in 1212, it took the name rue Saint-Thomas du Louvre in 1242" and cut the rest, or return null - the register entry is five short sentences and the summary has spent most of them.

issues: period: everything in the detail is 1808 or later - the course at suppression, the pre-1808 start, the Revolution name - and the 1212 rue des Chanoines and the 1242 rue Saint-Thomas-du-Louvre, the only pre-1550 facts in the source, are left to the summary. | voice: 45 words of register administration.
suggested_edit: Lead on the two medieval names and cut the pre-1808 course: "In 1212 it was the rue des Chanoines; from 1242 it took the name of the collegiate church of Saint-Thomas-du-Louvre, which stood on it."

issues: overclaim: "Bercy is shown as a feudal fortress with a donjon" drops two hedges at once - the source says the old plans show "une sorte de forteresse d'aspect feodal", a sort of fortress of feudal appearance. What the map shows is how the place looked, which is not the same as what it was.
suggested_edit: "On this map and other plans of the same years Bercy appears as a kind of fortress, feudal in look, with a keep inside a walled enclosure and a fortified gate near the Seine." Everything else in this entry is exact, including the forty horsemen and the windmill, and it is one of the best in the set.

issues: overclaim: "the village dominates the confluence of the Seine and Marne" is the detail's own reading of the sheet; the source says only what the old plans show the village to have consisted of - the church of Saint-Pierre and the remains of the Sejour de Bourgogne - and that they depict the territory schematically.
suggested_edit: "On this map the village is little more than the church of Saint-Pierre and the remains of the 14th-century Sejour de Bourgogne." The rest - 865, 1358, 11 January 1436, the Sejour du Roi with stables for fifty horses, Gillette Hennequin in 1481 - is exact and is among the best writing in the set.

issues: overclaim: "a parish survey recorded 47 households, or about 211 inhabitants" - the source says an archdeacon's visitation found the TWO parishes counting "environ 47 feux"; the detail drops "environ" from the households while keeping "about" for the inhabitants, and turns a visitation into a survey.
